hook: Severe drought across the Americas threatens 30 percent of cactus species.

sections.voiceover: Severe drought across the Americas threatens 30 percent of cactus species.
sections.visual_cue: Cinematic aerial shot of parched desert soil with cracked ground and solitary cactus under blazing sun
sections.sfx_cue: Low wind rumble and tense synth drone
b_roll: parched desert soil under harsh sun
sections.animation_cue: Slow push-in on cracked desert ground

sections.voiceover: On November 11, 2026, Michiel D. Pillet reported severe drought increases extinction risks. Threats have accelerated since the 2015 global assessment. Where can 1,000 species survive as desert ecosystems warm?
sections.visual_cue: Macro archival research visuals showing desert flora, field research journal data overlay
sections.sfx_cue: Subtle page turn sound and rising atmospheric hum

sections.voiceover: But the IUCN Cactus and Succulent Plants Specialist Group warns habitats won't stay suitable across the Americas.
sections.visual_cue: Dramatic wide angle shot of arid landscape fading from green scrubland to desolate dry earth
sections.animation_cue: Rapid zoom-out exposing vast dry expanse

sections.voiceover: Over a quarter of species will lose 80 percent of habitat by 2100. The Cactus and Succulent Society of America reports that poaching's accelerated dramatically since 2015.
sections.visual_cue: Data visualization showing regional habitat shrinkage across desert regions
sections.sfx_cue: Deep bass drop followed by subtle electronic clicks
b_roll: map of Americas showing climate threat zones
rare cactus species in native habitat
sections.animation_cue: Overlay graphic of habitat loss percentage counter rising to 80%

sections.voiceover: Researchers at the University of Arizona report 30 percent of cactus species face extinction.
sections.visual_cue: Stark silhouette of a solitary cactus against a dimming sunset horizon
sections.animation_cue: Slow fade out to dark horizon
